Abdou Salam Sisawo, Nashir Ngoobi, and 43 others reacted to a post: Alhamdulillah, I am honoured to have served as one of the panelists at the AL-QISC Alumni Leadership Forum 2026, organised by the Al-Qur’an and Islamic Club (AL-QISC), Albukhary International University (AIU).

The forum, themed “Leading with Faith and Legacy,” provided a meaningful platform for us as AL-QISC alumni to share our leadership experiences, challenges, lessons learned, and reflections with current students and aspiring student leaders.

My own AL-QISC journey began in 2022 when I served as Secretary, followed by my role as Vice President in the subsequent session. Looking back, AL-QISC was more than just a club for me. It was an environment where I learned about responsibility, teamwork, communication, service, and leadership.

One important lesson I shared during the forum is that leadership is not simply about holding a position; it is about the responsibility entrusted to us and the impact we leave behind.

I am grateful to AL-QISC and the organising committee for inviting me to be part of this meaningful forum. It was a privilege to reconnect with the AL-QISC community, reflect on my own leadership journey, and share experiences with the current generation of students.

May Allah bless the efforts of AL-QISC and all those who continue to serve the AIU community with Amanah, Ikhlas, and a spirit of service.

Sazally Manjang and Norpisah Mat Isa reacted to a post: From an idea discussed among students to an officially funded social business project. 🌱🇲🇱
I’m proud and grateful to share that our team, Shea Nafa (Mali), has been awarded RM15,000 through the Albukhary International University Social Business Seed Fund Grant.
This journey has been a valuable reminder that meaningful change often starts with a simple idea, but turning that idea into something practical requires teamwork, persistence, creativity, and the courage to keep developing it.
As a Social Development student, this experience has given me the opportunity to go beyond the classroom and learn through action. It has challenged me to think about how entrepreneurship can be connected to community development, local resources, and sustainable opportunities.
Most importantly, I’m grateful to my teammates for the effort, ideas, and commitment that brought us to this stage. This achievement belongs to the whole team.
RM15,000 is not the destination, it is the beginning.
Now comes the most important part: turning our idea into something meaningful and creating value for the community.
Proud to contribute to a project carrying the name of Mali 🇲🇱, while learning and building in Malaysia 🇲🇾.
Alhamdulillah for the opportunity.
